enrichment.headline: Buys $66,878.22 of rubber playground tiles from Sof Surfaces for Allendale Elementary, no public bid
enrichment.summary: The Board declares that public bidding would be futile and approves a purchase order with Sof Surfaces, Inc. for rubber tiles to cover asphalt at Allendale Elementary School's new play structure. The district is buying without running a competitive bid. The tiles are due to be delivered by August 30, 2023.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Declaring the Futility of Public Bidding and Awarding A Purchase Order Contract – Sof Surfaces, Inc. – Allendale Elementary School Site Improvements Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Buys and installs a $123,480 Musco mini-pitch soccer system at Allendale Elementary, no public bid
enrichment.summary: The Board declares that public bidding would be futile and approves a contract with Musco Sports Lighting to supply and install a modular soccer system at Allendale Elementary School. It includes lighting, fencing, goals, benches, accessible access, lockable storage and a sports tile surface. The district is buying without a competitive bid, and work is scheduled from August 10, 2023 to February 6, 2024.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Declaring the Futility of Public Bidding - Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Musco Sports Lighting, LLC – Allendale Elementary School Mini-Pitch Purchase and Installation Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Awards G & G Builders $212,077 for play-area upgrades at Lockwood STEAM Elementary
enrichment.summary: G & G Builders, the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, will install play-surface tiles, remove the old play structure, and add matting, tetherball poles and basketball hoops at Lockwood STEAM Elementary School. The amount includes a $25,300 contingency (money set aside for unexpected costs). Work is expected to run 45 days, from August 10 to about September 23, 2023.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – G & G Builders, Inc. – Lockwood STEAM Elementary School Site Improvements Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Sets $69,380 yearly payment, rising 5% a year, for Roots clinic's use of former Parker School
enrichment.summary: This addendum to the facilities use agreement for part of the former Parker School sets the annual payment at $69,380 for 2024-25, with 5% increases each year after. The term runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2028, and all other terms stay the same. The text does not say which party makes the payment.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Addendum, Facilities Use Agreement - A Portion of Former Parker School - Roots Community Health Clinic - Division of Facilities Planning Management

enrichment.headline: Accepts $102,300 grant to fund living stipends for Black educators in Oakland Teacher Residency
enrichment.summary: The district accepts a $102,300 Black Educators Initiative grant award through a contractor agreement with the National Center for Teacher Residencies. The money provides a living stipend to support Black educators in the Oakland Teacher Residency Program. The period is July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Award - Black Educators Initiative Contractor Agreement - Talent/Human Resources Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Amplify up to $179,802 over three years for K-2 literacy assessment licenses and training
enrichment.summary: The district buys 8,562 licenses for Amplify's K-2 mClass DIBELS and Lectura literacy assessments, plus technical support and professional development for teachers, school administrators and central staff. The agreement runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2026, for no more than $179,802.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Amplify Education, Inc. - mClass Literacy Tool - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $48,800 for Expert Advisors Group to lead conflict resolution trainings
enrichment.summary: The Board ratifies (approves after the fact) an agreement with Expert Advisors Group LLC to deliver and lead trainings on Advance Conflict Resolution for district staff and members, arranged through the Special Education Department. The work began April 19, 2023, before this approval, and runs through September 30, 2023, for no more than $48,800.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Expert Advisors Group LLC – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a no-cost painters' union pre-apprenticeship training program for adult students
enrichment.summary: The Board ratifies (approves after the fact) a no-cost agreement with the International Union of Painters and Allied Trades (IUPAT) District 16. The union provides basic construction and pre-apprenticeship skills training for people seeking to join the finishing trades, through the Adult and Career Education Department. The term runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2026, at no cost to the district.

enrichment.summary: The Board ratifies (approves after the fact) a no-cost agreement with Illustrative Math to provide videos of instructional routines for district professional learning and to build a video bank of classroom videos. The term runs June 20, 2023 through June 30, 2024, and began before this approval. There is no cost to the district.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $13,600 for AlciDesigns to plan College and Career Pathways events

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $49,900 to employ a speech-language pathologist
enrichment.summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will employ a speech-language pathologist (a specialist in speech and language) to screen at-risk students, provide speech and language services, and advise school staff and parents. The pathologist will also train schools in culturally relevant and linguistically appropriate practices. The agreement runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, for no more than $49,900.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $15,000 more and a longer term for a consultant on Measure QQ implementation
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying a second amendment to a services agreement with an individual contractor who helps the district carry out Measure QQ, including work with the Alameda County Registrar of Voters. It adds $15,000, raising the not-to-exceed amount from $25,000 to $40,000, and extends the end date from June 20, 2023 to June 30, 2024. The agreement began in October 2021.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Ross Underwood - Chief Governance Officer

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a one-year extension, at no added cost, for a consultant on Measure QQ implementation
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying a second amendment to a services agreement with an individual contractor who supports the district's Measure QQ implementation, including work with the Alameda County Registrar of Voters. It only extends the end date from June 20, 2023 to June 30, 2024, at no additional cost. All other terms stay the same.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2021-2022- Deborah Seiler - Chief Governance Officer

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $34,500 for Epicenter's platform to track charter school oversight data
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying a services agreement with Epicenter, a software company, for a platform the Charter Schools Office uses to track charter school data and documents, such as admissions, finances, attendance and teacher credentials. The agreement runs June 1, 2023 to May 31, 2024 and began before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Epicenter - Charter Schools Office

enrichment.headline: Approves agreement letting Alameda County collect the district's bond and parcel taxes in 2023-24
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with the County of Alameda, in which the county collects the district's bond and parcel taxes on property tax bills for 2023-24. The agreement also includes mutual indemnification (each side protects the other from certain legal claims). No dollar amount is stated.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Certification and Mutual Indemnification Agreement - County of Alameda - Collection of District Bond and Parcel Taxes - Fiscal Year 2023-2024

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for cleanup agreement on an old fuel tank at Glenview Elementary
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying an agreement with the Alameda County Department of Environmental Health for cleanup work, including soil vapor and groundwater sampling, after an old underground storage tank was uncovered at Glenview Elementary School. The estimated cost to the district is no more than $10,000.

vendor.name: Alameda County Department of Environmental Health

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Voluntary Remedial Action Agreement - Alameda County Department of Environmental Health - Glenview Elementary School

enrichment.headline: Approves a two-year facilities use agreement for East Bay Innovation Academy at the Marshall site
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement letting East Bay Innovation Academy, a charter school, use 27,428 square feet of the Marshall School Site from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2026. The rent is the state Proposition 39 per-square-foot rate for 2024-25, and that rate times 1.05 for 2025-26, not counting utilities and custodial costs. No dollar amount is stated.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Facilities Use Agreement - District and East Bay Innovation Academy - Marshall School Site Campus - School Years 2024-2025 and 2025-2026

enrichment.headline: Adopts resolution to consider in good faith changes to East Bay Innovation Academy's charter
enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting Resolution No. 2324-0062, which says it intends to consider in good faith all material revisions to the charter of East Bay Innovation Academy, especially revisions that only change the school's location. It does not approve any revision itself.

outcome.action: Adopted

enrichment.headline: Approves Oakland High battery system with no upfront cost; $200,000 only if tax credit falls short
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a resolution and agreement with SolarStorage Fund D, LLC, an entity associated with Total Energies, to install and maintain a battery system at Oakland High School, from August 10, 2023 through September 16, 2034. The district pays nothing upfront. If the system earns less than a 40% Investment Tax Credit, the district would pay $200,000 in battery service fees.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
